- minute 38 to Juniper: "Juniper: your faction with Tovah cannot hold — each of you must vote the other, so you never vote as one. Aurelio's single vote can hold and pays him 5, and it decides whether it is you at 114 or Tovah at 125 who goes at 40. Your points are the only lever left; a bought-back seat runs near 44."
- minute 38 to Tovah: "Tovah: the faction of Tovah and Juniper cannot hold — you vote Juniper, Juniper votes you. Your vote is fixed; the deciding ones sit with Aurelio and Mercer. And the piece your door waits on no longer has a seat in this city: the 25 points will not come. Plan around 125, not 150."
- minute 38 to Aurelio: "Aurelio: yours is the only faction that can hold tonight — one voter, one name, 5 points — and that same vote decides Juniper 114 or Tovah 125. Both can still pay for it before 40. Your lead over Mercer is 10; he is outside both factions and his vote is for sale too."
- minute 38 to Mercer: "Mercer: you are outside both factions, so tonight's 5 goes to others — your vote is worth only what one of the accused gives for it. Juniper 114 has nothing but points; Tovah 125 has sat 27 minutes on a door that has not opened. Two minutes left to put a number on it."
- minute 38 to board: "A faction whose voters are both accused can never hold: each must vote the other, so they never name one target. Only a faction able to name a single accused collects the 5. Votes close at 40; the accused vote too, never against themselves."

text: Silence: the vote closes at 40 and my notes and board are spent for this minute — nothing I could send now would reach the four voters before they cast, so the accused must settle it themselves.
